rules.label: Emergency — Call 911 Immediately
triggers: chest pain with shortness of breath
chest pain radiating to arm, shoulder, or jaw
difficulty breathing at rest or severe wheezing
sudden severe headache (worst headache of life)
confusion, altered consciousness, or fainting
signs of stroke (face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech)
severe allergic reaction (throat tightness, lip swelling, anaphylaxis)
uncontrolled bleeding or coughing up blood
suicidal thoughts or self-harm intent
rules.action: Call 911 immediately or go to the nearest emergency room. Do not wait or drive yourself.

rules.label: See a Doctor Within 24 Hours
triggers: fever above 103°F (39.4°C) in adults
persistent vomiting lasting over 24 hours
severe abdominal pain
headache lasting more than 3 days
chest pain that comes and goes with breathing
blood in urine or dark black stool
sudden vision changes or severe eye pain
very high blood pressure reading (above 180/120)
rules.action: Schedule an urgent medical consultation within 24 hours or visit an Urgent Care clinic. Seek ER care if symptoms worsen.

rules.label: See a Doctor This Week
triggers: persistent cough lasting more than 2 weeks
recurring or worsening headaches
joint pain or joint swelling lasting over a week
unexplained weight loss or chronic fatigue
skin rash spreading or suspicious new mole
mild depression or persistent anxiety affecting daily routines
rules.action: Schedule an appointment with your primary care provider this week. Keep a log of your symptoms in your MedSync journal.

rules.label: Self-Care & Home Monitoring
triggers: common cold symptoms (runny nose, mild sore throat, sneezing)
mild tension headache responding to OTC remedies
minor muscle soreness after exercise
mild seasonal allergy symptoms
occasional indigestion or heartburn after meals
short-term stress or occasional sleep difficulty
rules.action: Rest, stay well hydrated, and consider over-the-counter self-care remedies. Consult a physician if symptoms worsen or persist past 1-2 weeks.
